script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. AFFluENT SUBURBAN NEIGHBORHOOD - DAY

The sun sets behind a row of modern houses, their windows aglow. A crisp autumn breeze rustles the leaves.

INT. LIVING ROOM - SAM'S HOUSE - DAY

SAM (16, wearing basketball shorts and a t-shirt) sits on the couch, staring at a basketball hoop in his living room. His mother, MRS. JENKINS (mid-40s, dressed casually), enters.

MRS. JENKINS: Sam, you've been in there all day. Go outside and play.

SAM: Mom, I can't. My friends all go to private schools. They don't live around here.

MRS. JENKINS: (smiling) Well, then make some new friends. Go outside and see who's around.

Sam nods, stands up, and exits the house.

EXT. NEIGHBORHOOD STREET - DAY

Sam wanders the neighborhood, looking for someone to play basketball with. He passes by a group of kids playing soccer in a driveway, but they're too engrossed in their game to notice him. He approaches a park, but the courts are empty.

Just as Sam is about to give up, he hears laughter coming from the end of the street. He follows the sound and finds a boy, MIKE (16, wearing soccer cleats and a t-shirt), practicing soccer alone.

SAM: (calling out) Hey, do you mind if I watch? I've never really played soccer before.

MIKE: (turning around, surprised) Oh, hey there. Sure thing.

They make small talk as Sam watches Mike practice, and before long, Mike invites Sam to try playing with him. They spend the rest of the afternoon learning each other's games and sharing stories.

INT. LIVING ROOM - SAM'S HOUSE - EVENING

Sam enters the house, beaming with excitement.

MRS. JENKINS: (from the kitchen) Hey, Sam, how was your day?

SAM: (grinning) Mom, you won't believe it. I met this kid, Mike, and we played basketball and soccer all afternoon!

MRS. JENKINS: (smiling) That's wonderful, Sam. It's important to make new friends and try new things.

EXT. PARK - DAY

The sun rises over the park as Sam and Mike practice their games together. They laugh and encourage each other, their friendship growing stronger with each passing day.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY

Sam and Mike stand on opposite sides of the basketball court, facing off against each other and their respective teams. The crowd cheers as the game begins.

Despite their rivalry on the court, their friendship remains unshaken. They exchange high-fives and friendly banter, knowing that their bond goes beyond the game.

INT. LIVING ROOM - SAM'S HOUSE - NIGHT

Sam sits on the couch, watching a basketball game on TV. Mike enters, wearing his basketball uniform.

MIKE: Hey, Sam, want to come out and shoot some hoops with me?

SAM: (smiling) I'd love to, but I've got a big paper due tomorrow. Why don't you come in and help me study instead?

Mike sits down next to Sam and they spend the evening working on their homework together, their friendship providing the motivation and support they need to succeed.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY

The stands are filled with families and friends as Sam and Mike's teams face off in the championship game. The tension is palpable, but their friendship remains strong.

In the final moments of the game, with the score tied, Sam and Mike find themselves on the court together. They exchange a knowing glance and, without a word, pass the ball back and forth, each waiting for the other to make the winning shot.

As the buzzer sounds, Sam makes a move towards the basket, and Mike delivers a perfect assist. Sam sinks the shot, and the crowd erupts in cheers.

Sam turns to Mike and hugs him, their teammates and opponents joining in the celebration of their friendship.

FADE OUT.
